title: Logical Operators and Short-Circuit Evaluation
learningObjectives: Explain the key idea in logical operators and short-circuit evaluation.
Identify the relevant syntax and rules.
Trace each example and predict the result.
Apply the concept in a small program.
Avoid a common mistake related to this topic.

understand.concept: Logical operators combine or negate boolean expressions. `&&` requires both conditions to be true, `||` requires at least one, and `!` negates a condition. Short-circuit evaluation may skip the right operand.
understand.whyItMatters: Combining checks helps validate inputs and express multi-part requirements while avoiding unsafe evaluation order.
understand.analogy: Think of this as a control or calculation rule that tells a program how to handle a particular situation consistently.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only a starting point; C++ syntax, types and execution rules determine actual behaviour.
understand.explain:
## Operators
`&&` (AND), `||` (OR) and `!` (NOT) work with boolean expressions.

## Short-circuit
For `&&`, the right side is not evaluated when the left side is false. For `||`, it is not evaluated when the left side is true. This can be used to guard checks, such as testing a pointer before dereferencing it.

## Readability
Use parentheses and avoid overly complex conditions. Break complex logic into named boolean variables when that makes intent clearer.
